name: 23.976 fps (often shown as 23.98)
used_for: North American HDTV and 'NTSC film' (24p material in 60 Hz-derived systems)
timecode: Non-drop frame only; no drop-frame variant exists

name: 25 fps
used_for: PAL and SECAM regions (Europe, Australia, parts of South America), DVB; also allowed in ATSC
timecode: Non-drop frame; 50i broadcast carries 25 interlaced frames per second

name: 29.97 fps non-drop (NDF)
used_for: NTSC regions (US, Canada, Mexico, Colombia et al.), ATSC, PAL-M (Brazil)
timecode: Counts 30 frame numbers per second continuously, so one hour of 29.97 NDF timecode runs 3.6 s longer than wall-clock time; 00:59:56:12 NDF equals 01:00:00;00 DF
notes: Apple's iTunes film spec notes many software systems use the imprecise ratio 30/999×1000 instead of the precise 30000/1001.

name: 29.97 fps drop frame (DF)
used_for: Broadcast deliveries in NTSC regions where timecode must match clock time
timecode: Skips frame NUMBERS 00 and 01 at the start of every minute except minutes divisible by 10 (00, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50): 18 numbers per 10 minutes, 108 per hour, so one hour holds 107,892 frames instead of 108,000. No picture frames are removed. Residual drift about 1 frame every 9 h 15 min. Written with a semicolon (or period) before the frames: HH:MM:SS;FF
notes: Example sequence: 01:08:59;29 is followed by 01:09:00;02, but 01:09:59;29 is followed by 01:10:00;00. Apple's spec requires the semicolon after the seconds for drop-frame mode.

name: 30 fps
used_for: ATSC; common web/phone capture rate (YouTube lists 30 as common)

name: 50 fps
used_for: 50 Hz (PAL-derived) HD progressive systems (BT.709 50/P); high-frame-rate web uploads (YouTube lists 50 as common)

name: 59.94 fps
used_for: 60 Hz-derived (NTSC-region) HD progressive (BT.709 60/1.001); also the field rate of 1080i/480i NTSC broadcast
timecode: Drop-frame variant exists: skips 4 frame numbers at each affected minute boundary (same every-minute-except-tenth rule as 29.97 DF)
notes: The 4-frame figure comes from industry sources; the SMPTE ST 12 text itself (paywalled) was not opened.

name: 60 fps
used_for: 60 Hz HD progressive (BT.709 60/P); high-frame-rate web uploads (YouTube lists 60 as common)
